data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism description ends with the assertion: 'Unlike every previously studied system of this kind, which faced identical structural constraints yet exhibited none of this behaviour.' This is a universal novelty claim that is internally self-contradictory. The target's entire argument is that the preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible 'on Popper's own terms' — meaning the mechanism IS Popper's critical rationalism, a previously and extensively studied system of exactly this kind (theory-selection via severe testing without inductive justification). Popper's system did exhibit precisely 'this behaviour': preferring theories that survived severe tests while treating corroboration as a report of past performance rather than a predictor of future reliability. The target cannot coherently claim to be articulating Popper's own framework while simultaneously asserting that no previously studied system of this kind exhibited the behaviour it describes. Either the mechanism is Popper's (in which case the novelty claim is false), or it is a novel departure (in which case the claim that it is defensible 'on Popper's own terms' is undermined). No evidence, derivation, or reference is provided to support this sweeping empirical claim about 'every previously studied system,' making it an unsupported assertion appended to the core argument.
